nodes.name: Download from Google Drive
nodes.notes: Downloads the file's binary content from Google Drive so the next node can parse it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Parse PDF Contents
nodes.notes: Parses the incoming PDF binary into JSON items.

nodes.name: Clean & Reshape Rows
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming document records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Load Rows into Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Document Tracker', matched on documentId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

# Extract from uploaded files for invoices

**Pattern:** File Processing · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers invoices work end to end across Google Sheets and Google Drive.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Download from Google Drive
3. Parse PDF Contents
4. Clean & Reshape Rows
5. Load Rows into Google Sheets
6. Align Field Names
7. Cap Batch Volume
8. Save Execution Metadata
9. Stamp Processing Time

## Why it exists

Doing invoices work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Download from Google Drive → Parse PDF Contents → Clean & Reshape Rows → Load Rows into Google Sheets → Align Field Names → Cap Batch Volume → Save Execution Metadata → Stamp Processing Time

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Google Drive aligned by hand for invoices
- Invoices work where "Download from Google Drive" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Invoices work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Google Drive in step for invoices, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Google Drive call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this invoices build
- Every invoices run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for invoices before wiring Google Sheets
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for invoices

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Bad rows are quarantined into their own store, not dropped silently and not allowed to break the whole batch — one malformed row in a 10,000-row file shouldn't stop the other 9,999 from loading, but it also shouldn't vanish without a trace.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Feed it a file with a few deliberately malformed rows and confirm they land in quarantine, not the main store.
2. Switch the source format (e.g. csv to xlsx) and see how little actually has to change.
3. Turn on archive mode and confirm the processed file gets repacked and stored.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your invoices process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole invoices payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
